deep.reconstruction:
PROBLEM (the next page makes the context explicit). Take pi = alpha^r beta^s in a product of two cyclic groups of orders a and b. Put rho = r/a and sigma = s/b, and define pi_1, rho_1, sigma_1 the same way. The common elements pi^x = pi_1^{x_1} correspond to the integer pairs (x, x_1) with rho x ≡ rho_1 x_1, sigma x ≡ sigma_1 x_1, x ≡ 0, 0 ≡ x_1 (mod 1). In modern terms: P = (rho, sigma) and P_1 = (rho_1, sigma_1) are points of (Q/Z)^2, and the task is to determine the cyclic group

∩ . The notation [a, b, ...] is Dedekind's gcd of rational numbers, i.e. the generator of the Z-module they span. (1) ORDERS. [rho, sigma, 1] = 1/w, so w is the order of P. Put u = w rho and v = w sigma; these are integers with gcd(u, v, w) = 1. Likewise [rho_1, sigma_1, 1] = 1/w_1 with u_1, v_1. Substitute y = x/w and y_1 = x_1/w_1. The system becomes u y ≡ u_1 y_1, v y ≡ v_1 y_1, w y ≡ 0, w_1 y_1 ≡ 0 (mod 1). (2) ELIMINATING y_1. Choose integers l, m, n with u_1 l + v_1 m + w_1 n = 1 and put h = u l + v m. - Combine: l·(first) + m·(second) − n·(w_1 y_1 ≡ 0). This gives h y ≡ y_1. [This combination step is mine.] - The system is then equivalent to: (u − h u_1) y ≡ 0, (v − h v_1) y ≡ 0, w y ≡ 0, h w_1 y ≡ 0. - Hence it is equivalent to p y ≡ 0, with p = gcd(u − h u_1, v − h v_1, h w_1, w). (3) KEY LEMMA: p = p_1 := gcd(w, w_1, w_2), where w_2 = u v_1 − v u_1. - First, p_1 = gcd(w_2, w u_1, w v_1, u w_1, v w_1, w w_1) = gcd(w_2, w, w_1), because gcd(u, v, w) = gcd(u_1, v_1, w_1) = 1. - p_1 divides p. Using the Bezout relation one gets u − h u_1 = m w_2 + n u w_1 and v − h v_1 = −l w_2 + n v w_1. So all four generators of p are divisible by p_1. - p divides p_1. We have w_2 = (u − h u_1) v_1 − (v − h v_1) u_1 ≡ 0 and w ≡ 0 (mod p). Moreover (u − h u_1) w_1 + h w_1 u_1 = u w_1 ≡ 0, similarly v w_1 ≡ 0, and w w_1 ≡ 0. Hence w_1 = w_1·gcd(u, v, w) ≡ 0 (mod p). - Therefore p = p_1 = [w, w_1, w_2]. - A struck line l(u − h u_1) + m(v − h v_1) + n(−h w_1) = h − h = 0 is an abandoned check. (4) GENERAL SOLUTION. Write p y = z (an integer) and w = c p, w_1 = c_1 p, w_2 = c_2 p. - Then x = (w/p) z and y_1 = h y + z_1, so x_1 = (w_1/p)(h z + p z_1), with z and z_1 arbitrary integers. - Here h is characterised mod p by h u_1 ≡ u, h v_1 ≡ v, h w_1 ≡ 0 (mod p). These congruences determine h uniquely mod p because gcd(u_1, v_1, w_1) = 1 [this remark is mine]. - Since p | w and gcd(u, v, w) = 1, we get gcd(u, v, p) = 1, hence gcd(h, p) = 1. So h h_1 + p p' = 1 for suitable h_1, p'. - Two generating solutions: - z = 1, z_1 = 0 gives (x, x_1) = (w/p, h w_1/p); - z = h_1, z_1 = p' gives (x, x_1) = (h_1 w/p, w_1/p). - So

∩ is cyclic of order p, generated by c·P = (h c_1)·P_1. A struck attempt h x_1 = (1 − p p') (w_1/p) z + ... is abandoned. (5) BOXES AND BOTTOM (module formulation). Here the roles of c and c_1 are interchanged: w = c_1 p_2, w_1 = c p_2, w_2 = k_2 p_2, and p_2 = p = p_1. - rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1 = w_2/(w w_1) = k_2/(c c_1 p). - gcd(k_2, c, c_1) = 1. - Put M = [rho, sigma, 1] = 1/(c_1 p), M_1 = [rho_1, sigma_1, 1] = 1/(c p), and M_2 = [rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1, rho, sigma, rho_1, sigma_1, 1] = [rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1, M, M_1]. - Multiplying by w w_1 gives w w_1 M_2 = gcd(w_2, u w_1, v w_1, w u_1, w v_1, w w_1) = p_1 = p. Hence M_2 = p M M_1 = 1/(c c_1 p). - Consequently M = c M_2 and M_1 = c_1 M_2. - Directly: M_2 = [w_2/(c c_1 p^2), 1/(c_1 p), 1/(c p)] = (M_2/p)·[w_2, c p, c_1 p]. Hence p = [w_2, c p, c_1 p] and 1 = [w_2/p, c, c_1]. - Interpretation: 1/M_2 = w w_1/p is the order of , and 1/M_2 equals 1 over the gcd of the 2x2 minors of the matrix (1 0 rho rho_1; 0 1 sigma sigma_1). errors: No mathematical error found. Every identity checked: u − h u_1 = m w_2 + n u w_1, v − h v_1 = −l w_2 + n v w_1, w_2 = (u − h u_1) v_1 − (v − h v_1) u_1, and w w_1·[rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1, rho, sigma, rho_1, sigma_1, 1] = p.

Notational inconsistency, not an error. The middle section sets w = c p, w_1 = c_1 p. The bottom section and right boxes use w = c_1 p_2, w_1 = c p_2 (so [rho, sigma, 1] = c·M_2 = 1/(c_1 p)). Read with the earlier convention, '[rho, sigma, 1] = c[...]' would be wrong; with the box convention it is correct.

The step h y ≡ y_1 is stated without derivation. It follows from l·(first) + m·(second) − n·(w_1 y_1 ≡ 0). The converse (that the reduced system implies the original) is also left implicit but is immediate from y_1 := h y + z_1.
Two struck lines are abandoned attempts and carry no claims.

results.what:
For P = (rho, sigma) and P_1 = (rho_1, sigma_1) in (Q/Z)^2 of orders w and w_1 (u = w rho, etc.), the intersection

∩ is cyclic of order p = gcd(w, w_1, u v_1 − v u_1). The proof eliminates x_1 by a Bezout combination.
results.modern_name: Order of the intersection of two cyclic subgroups of a finite abelian group (rank ≤ 2); special case of determinantal divisors / Smith normal form
results.usually_credited_to: Elementary consequence of Smith (1861) / Frobenius–Stickelberger (1878–79) theory of invariant factors; folklore

results.what: Explicit parametrisation of all integer solutions (x, x_1) of the simultaneous congruences: x = (w/p) z, x_1 = (w_1/p)(h z + p z_1), where h is determined mod p and gcd(h, p) = 1. Generators are (w/p, h w_1/p) and (h_1 w/p, w_1/p).
results.modern_name: Solution of a system of linear congruences / Hermite normal form of the solution lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss / H.J.S. Smith (systems of linear congruences)

results.what: [rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1, rho, sigma, rho_1, sigma_1, 1] = p·[rho, sigma, 1]·[rho_1, sigma_1, 1]. That is, the gcd of the 2x2 minors gives the order w w_1/p of the group <P, P_1>, using Dedekind's gcd-of-rationals (module) notation.
results.modern_name: Index of a lattice = inverse of gcd of maximal minors (second determinantal divisor)
results.usually_credited_to: H.J.S. Smith (1861); Dedekind's module notation [a, b, ...] is his own (Dirichlet–Dedekind Supplement XI)

deep.surprise_reason: This is clean but elementary number theory: linear congruences mod 1 and the gcd-of-minors formula for the order of a subgroup of (Q/Z)^2, written in Dedekind's characteristic module-gcd notation. It is fully consistent with his known style and with standard 19th-century theory (Smith, Frobenius–Stickelberger). The group-theoretic motivation (intersection of cyclic subgroups in a product of two cyclic groups) is mildly interesting as context, but not novel.

checkable.asserts: u − h u_1 = w_2 m + u w_1 n whenever u_1 l + v_1 m + w_1 n = 1, with h = u l + v m.
v − h v_1 = −w_2 l + v w_1 n under the same Bezout relation.
w_2 = (u − h u_1) v_1 − (v − h v_1) u_1 for arbitrary h.
w w_1 (rho sigma_1 − sigma rho_1) = u v_1 − v u_1 = w_2.
